body:
An ultra-photorealistic wildlife photograph capturing the exact split second a vibrant blue-and-orange kingfisher dives vertically into a calm lake to catch a small fish.

Its long, sharp beak has just broken through the water surface, creating a tiny circular splash with delicate water droplets suspended in mid-air.

The kingfisher's wings are fully extended symmetrically, revealing hundreds of individually detailed feathers. Its reflection is visible beneath the water, slightly distorted by expanding ripples.

Warm golden-hour sunlight illuminates the feathers from behind, creating beautiful translucent feather edges. Dark, creamy green and golden bokeh background.

Extreme wildlife photography, shot on a professional 600mm telephoto lens, incredibly sharp subject, realistic water physics, natural anatomy, precise details, cinematic depth of field.

The exact instant of impact, not before or after. No illustration, no CGI appearance.

Ratio: 1:1
